title: Best-Seeing Nights Ranking
dataSources: Observatory environment (`observatory:env`), sky-quality meter (`skyquality:reading`), imaging sessions (`imaging:session`), telescope mount (`mount:status`), cloud sensor (`allsky:cloud`).
app: Backyard observatory automation — roll-off-roof/dome controller, sky-quality meter, cloud sensor, telescope mount, and astrophotography capture software (N.I.N.A./Ekos) — logging to Splunk HEC via MQTT and scripted inputs.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=mount:status
| bin _time span=1d
| stats avg(guide_rms_arcsec) as rms, min(guide_rms_arcsec) as best by _time
| sort rms
| head 10
description: Ranks your calmest, steadiest nights by guiding performance so you can plan demanding targets for similar conditions.
value: Atmospheric steadiness makes or breaks planetary and fine detail; knowing your best nights helps you recognise and use them.
implementation: Ingest nightly guiding statistics; rank nights by average steadiness.
visualization: Ranked table of nights by guiding steadiness.
detailedImplementation:
## Prerequisites

• **Splunk**: Splunk Enterprise ≥9.0 or Splunk Cloud — a single-instance home lab is fine. Create `index=personal` with 90–365 day retention (`indexes.conf`).
• **HEC token**: Settings → Data Inputs → HTTP Event Collector → New Token → index `personal`. Store the token in your connector's environment (never commit it to git).
• **Upstream product**: Personal HEC index — HTTP Event Collector token on index=personal.
• **Subcategory context**: Backyard Astronomy & Observatory — typical feeds: Observatory environment (`observatory:env`), sky-quality meter (`skyquality:reading`), imaging sessions (`imaging:session`), telescope mount (`mount:status`), cloud sensor (`allsky:cloud`)..
• **Sourcetypes in this search**: `mount:status`.
• **Network**: The connector host must reach both the vendor API/MQTT broker and your Splunk HEC port (8088/tcp).

## Step 1 — Configure data collection

Route **Personal HEC index** events into `index=personal` with `sourcetype=mount:status`.

**Collection method:** HTTP Event Collector token on index=personal.

**Reference endpoint / path:** `POST https://<splunk>:8088/services/collector/event`.

**Suggested poll interval:** depends on upstream connector.

**Key fields to extract:** `sourcetype-specific — see search filters`.

**Typical connector stack:** Backyard observatory automation — roll-off-roof/dome controller, sky-quality meter, cloud sensor, telescope mount, and astrophotography software (N.I.N.A./Ekos) — via MQTT and scripted inputs..

**Author notes:** Ingest nightly guiding statistics; rank nights by average steadiness.


Example HEC payload shape:

```json
{"index": "personal", "sourcetype": "mount:status", "event": { ... vendor fields ... }}
```

Verify ingestion with:

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=mount:status earliest=-24h | head 20
```

## Step 2 — Create the search and alert

This search implements **Best-Seeing Nights Ranking** over `personal` data (primarily `sourcetype=mount:status`) across the full search range. The `avg, min` aggregation groups by `_time`; change the `by` clause if you want per-device, per-room, or per-user breakdowns instead.

**Fields this search depends on:** `_time`. Confirm each is populated before scheduling alerts.

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=mount:status
| bin _time span=1d
| stats avg(guide_rms_arcsec) as rms, min(guide_rms_arcsec) as best by _time
| sort rms
| head 10
```

## Step 3 — Validate

**(a) Compare to vendor UI:** Splunk Search → index=personal | stats count by sourcetype. Totals for the same day/week should match within connector lag (usually one poll interval).

**(b) Field presence:**

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=mount:status earliest=-7d
| head 50
| table _time
```

Every column the detection uses should be non-null on recent rows.

**(c) Volume sanity:**

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=mount:status earliest=-30d
| timechart span=1d count
```

Flatlines usually mean a broken token, expired OAuth refresh, or HEC URL change.

## Step 4 — Operationalize

Create a companion dashboard titled `UC-25.22.7: Personal evidence` with the following panel layout:

**Panel 1 — Ranked Table Of Nights By Guiding Steadiness (the key fields):** Configure according to standard Splunk visualization patterns for this panel type.


Time picker defaults: set to last 30 days with named presets for 24h, 7d, 30d, 90d, and 1y — the auditor needs all five windows without retyping. Enable scheduled PDF export for the full dashboard on the regulation's reporting cadence.

## Step 5 — Troubleshooting

**Personal HEC index — no Personal HEC index events / missing fields:** If `mount:status` stops updating, re-check HEC token, index `personal`, and firewall to port 8088. Search `index=_internal sourcetype=splunkd group=http_event_collector` for rejection reasons. Confirm the Personal HEC index connector script is still running (`systemctl status` or cron log).

**Personal HEC index — NULL values in extracted fields:** The Personal HEC index JSON export shape drifted — compare a raw event (`index=personal sourcetype=mount:status | head 1 | spath`) against the field names in Step 2. Re-map in the connector before changing the SPL.

**Personal HEC index — API error / auth denied (401/403):** Refresh tokens expire on most consumer APIs — re-authorize the scripted input, update `passwords.conf` / env vars, and verify the vendor developer app is not in sandbox mode.

**Personal HEC index — endpoint timeout / HTTP 429 throttling:** Back off the poll interval in the connector; Personal HEC index APIs often cap requests per 15 minutes on free tiers.

**Bucket misalignment:** `span=1d` buckets on UTC by default — if your routine is local-time based, add `| eval _time=_time + (local_offset)` or use `@d` / `@w` snap.

**Stale dashboard:** Confirm the saved search `dispatch.earliest_time` covers enough history for your `1d` buckets.
